decisions.reason: As an extension of an established sports-flooring business, it can still be carried with the firm's broad product range and organisational slack, though its fit with the firm's increasingly interior-focused direction makes it only moderately secure.

A mobile arena floor is a specialized and likely more volatile line, and if its post-launch results fell short of aspiration levels the firm would reallocate resources toward stronger core flooring activities.

This second mobile arena system appears similarly niche and potentially duplicative, so under bounded rationality and problemistic search it is a strong candidate for pruning if performance has been merely mediocre.

The chevron parquet sits very close to the firm's core offer and stated future direction and was presented as a flagship, so management would likely judge it as meeting aspirations or worth continued support.

A squash-court surface finish is a narrow specialist product, and in a firm shifting emphasis toward trend-led residential and interior flooring it is more likely to be dropped if returns are not clearly satisfactory.
As a low-complexity complementary accessory for existing sports floors, oak skirting is relatively cheap to keep on the market and can be retained even if demand is modest.
